blockers.title: Provider sync work is a hand-rolled lease queue and the repository has no queue extension decision anywhere
blockers.severity: architecture; not a defect and not a launch blocker on its own
blockers.diagnosis: MEASURED SURFACE: three indexes support the lease claim — `idx_event_sync_jobs_dedupe_active` (unique, partial on active), `idx_event_sync_jobs_claim` on `(status, run_after, priority, id) where status = 'queued'` (exactly the worker's sort order, and proven USABLE by the harness under `set enable_seqscan = off`), and `idx_event_sync_jobs_stale_locks` on `(locked_at) where status = 'running'`. The claim is a compare-and-set (`.eq('id', …).eq('status','queued')`), so two workers cannot both win a job. The retry ladder is `attempt_count`/`max_attempts` with `min(60_000 * 2**attempt_count, 30 min)` backoff and a `dead` terminal state, and `429`/retryable errors go back to `queued` with a delay so a provider rate limit cannot cause a storm. There is no visibility timeout process, no dead-letter table, and no admin retry surface beyond `admin/event-sync`'s read-only listing — a `dead` job is listed but nothing re-enqueues it. That is the real gap in the mechanism, and it is a product decision rather than a schema one.
blockers.why_not_repaired: A `create extension` in a migration is an irreversible cluster-level change to every environment, and the archived contract — which is the only contract this lane was given — names no extension. Choosing one here would be a transcription lane making an architecture decision.
blockers.requested_action: orchestrator, on ORCH-004: decide and record whether provider sync work stays a lease table or moves to `pgmq`. If it stays, the concrete follow-up is a dead-letter re-enqueue surface and a visibility timeout, which are application-side. If it moves, it is a forward additive migration plus a worker rewrite, and the two restored relations become the pgmq payload contract rather than the queue itself.

title: Two decisions DB-021 deliberately did not take: the provider-sync queue mechanism (lease table vs pgmq) and the CP-016 regeneration of two chain-ahead relations
summary: DB-021 authored 20260927140100_event_sync_jobs.sql, restoring the second of two relations from the archived 20260804130000 provider-foundation file. Two decisions were DELIBERATELY not taken by the transcription lane and are routed here rather than settled silently. (1) QUEUE MECHANISM. The archive's own comment at :94 calls event_sync_jobs a 'durable queue ... claimed by cron workers', so a queue is implied — but the archive names no extension, nothing in the 322-file active chain names one, and `pgmq` appears nowhere in this repository. What the archive actually specifies is a hand-rolled LEASE queue: `locked_at`/`locked_by` with a compare-and-set claim at cron/events/sync:79-86, `attempt_count`/`max_attempts` with bounded exponential backoff capped at 30 minutes, and `dead` as a terminal state. DB-021 transcribed that contract verbatim and added NO `create extension`, because a transcription lane pulling a queue extension into the chain is exactly the scope expansion this lane is chartered to refuse. The question of whether Tourify should standardise on `pgmq` for provider sync work is a real one and it is not answered here. (2) CP-016 REGENERATION. After DB-020 and DB-021 the chain is TWO relations AHEAD of `lib/database.types.ts`: `event_provider_connections` and `event_sync_jobs` both appear in the chain-only list of `node supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs .`. That is the SAFE direction — the chain is a superset, so regeneration may only ADD coverage and delete nothing — but the regeneration itself remains blocked on RELEASE-013 provisioning a chain-built target, and `--linked` must never be used as a source (CP-127). `lib/database.types.ts` is byte-unchanged at 168daaff01fb7ef285fb7bc69cfb5876cb092491953cdbbb2cea3fa7cb7558ab7 and is not hand-edited. Worth stating precisely: because all consumers of BOTH relations use an untyped service-role client, they emit NO tsc diagnostic, so there are no diagnostics to clear for this pair and none is claimed.
